coverage_notes:
WHAT IS SOLID. The head coach and the complete nine-man on-field assistant tier (the NCAA maximum in 1998) are fully recovered and independently corroborated: Wikipedia's roster-footer staff list for the team-season, cross-checked against archived utsports.com official staff bios captured by the Wayback Machine from the URL path /News+Release/Football/1998/07/06/, which is the exact "Staff" link target used by Tennessee's own football site during the 1998 season (verified from the Dec. 1, 1998 capture of utsports.com/teams/fbc/index.html, whose INFO CENTER dropdown points "Staff" at /News+Release/Football/1998/07/06/fbc_coaching_staff.html). Seven of those bios (Fulmer, Washington, Barry, Brooks, Caldwell, Chavis, Sanders) survive and explicitly reference the 1998 national championship season.

TWO RING-RULE EXCEPTIONS, BOTH FLAGGED. David Cutcliffe (OC/AHC/QB) left for the Ole Miss head job in December 1998 and did NOT coach the Jan. 4, 1999 Fiesta Bowl; Randy Sanders moved from running backs to offensive coordinator and called the plays in the title game. Kurt Roper, the lone documented graduate assistant, reportedly followed Cutcliffe to Ole Miss while Tennessee was preparing for the championship game, though his own infobox still credits him with Tennessee through 1998. Both are included with midseason_note; neither is clean under a strict "on staff at the championship game" rule.

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER — BE AWARE THIS LIST IS INCOMPLETE BELOW THE ON-FIELD TIER.
1. No 1998 Tennessee football media guide exists on archive.org (their holdings jump from 1954 to 1999), and no 1998-season Wayback capture of Tennessee's staff-directory page survives — every surviving capture of that URL was taken in 2000-2001 and shows the 1999/2000 staff. The SEC's 1998 conference handbook has a Tennessee preview but no staff roster. So there is NO contemporaneous 1998 staff directory for the support tiers.
2. All support-tier rows (Stucky, Altizer, Rollo, Frazier, Parrott) except Holloway rest on tenure statements in the 1999 media guide or in 1999-dated archived bios ("in his sixth year", "since 1994", "1992-present", "15th year/season") rather than on a 1998-dated roster. That is real documented evidence, not a guess, but it is one inferential step removed. Holloway is the exception: his hire is documented by a UT release dated 4/21/98 archived in May 1998.
3. GRADUATE ASSISTANTS: only Kurt Roper is documented. Tennessee would have carried at least two GAs; the second (and any volunteer/student assistants) is unrecoverable. The 1999 guide's GAs, Ryan Held and Shawn Quinn, are explicitly NOT 1998 staff or unprovable — Quinn "joined the Tennessee staff last spring" (spring 1999), and Held's bio only establishes he coached at Nebraska in 1996-97 and graduated in 1998.
4. STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING: only John Stucky is defensible. The 1999 guide's other S&C staff are excluded for lack of 1998 evidence — Brian Brown explicitly arrived "to Tennessee this spring" (1999); Chris Carlisle's bio gives no Tennessee start date; Johnny Long's bio gives no start date; Dan Eason's bio says he directed the strength program at Chowan College "from 1996 to 1998", which does not establish when he reached Knoxville. Including any of them would be padding.
5. ANALYST and QUALITY CONTROL: no rows. These were not staff categories in 1998 college football, and nothing in any source describes such a position at Tennessee.
6. MEDICAL: only head trainer Mike Rollo. Team physician Dr. Val Gene Iven, team orthopedist Dr. Bill Youmans, and assistant trainers John Christofferson and Chad Newman appear only in the 1999 guide with no statement placing them on the 1998 football staff (and Newman's entry says he "devotes most of his time working with the b[asketball] team"), so they are excluded.
7. NOT INCLUDED AT ALL, though named in the 1999 guide with zero 1998 tenure evidence: football video staff (Barry Rice, Joe Harrington, Link Eldson), data integrity clerk Glen Grimes, community relations administrative assistant Kevin Avery, and the football secretarial staff (Stacey Boyd, Pat Pryor, Kim Milligan, and a recruiting secretary whose first name OCRs as "Angela Sc-"). These are real 1999 names; asserting them for 1998 would be padding.
8. David Blackburn's listed title is the one he was promoted to in the winter AFTER the 1998 season. The source proves he was on Fulmer's staff doing football administration during 1998 but does not give his 1998 title.

SOURCE-QUALITY WARNING FOR MECHANICAL MATCHING. Quotes attributed to archive.org/download/tennessee-football-1999-media-guide/...djvu.txt come from an OCR scan of poor quality; they are copied byte-for-byte from that text file, artifacts and all, and are confined to a single line of that file to avoid line-break mismatches. Wikipedia quotes from the coaching-staff list use an en dash (U+2013) as the name/role separator and are trimmed at wikilink boundaries where necessary. Wayback Machine URLs must be fetched using the "+" (not "%20") form of the path — the "%20" captures of these same pages are archived 404s and return nothing. Mark Bradley and Kevin Ramsey have no surviving 1998-dated official Tennessee bio for this reason; their rows rest on Wikipedia plus, respectively, the 1999 media guide and Fiesta Bowl game coverage naming Ramsey as defensive backs coach at the title game.
